newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Latin American ADRs rise with Dow.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Latin American ADRs rise with Dow.

text.p: Latin American shares rose on weak U.S. volumes Friday, bolstered by short-covering and strength in the Dow after U.S. jobs data eased fears of an immediate rise in interest rates.
"Investors were positioned for a really bad unemployment number, but it wasn't as strong as what some people were afraid of," a trader said.

The Labor Department reported non-farm payrolls rose 250,000 in August, slightly higher than the 244,000 forecast by economists. The U.S. unemployment rate fell to 5.1 percent, lower than the expected 5.3 percent rate.

"Some of the locals were short in advance of the unemployment number. I think you may have got some locals trying to trade the U.S. market to cover themselves. Telebras, for example, felt like short-covering," the trader said.
The Brazilian blue chip's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) jumped 1-7/8 to 75-5/8 by early afternoon.
Argentine ADRs also posted strong gains, boosted by optimism that President Carlos Menem would find a way to implement his government's fiscal reform package.
Menem appealed to Peronist leaders on Thursday to close ranks and support his labor reforms.
"There's more of a consensus that Menem's going to rally the troops and push the reforms through," a trader said.
Argentina's YPF gained 3/8 to 22-1/8, while Telefonica added 1/2 to 23-7/8 and Banco Frances rose 3/4 to 23-3/4.
BAESA continued to recover lost ground after its recent retreat, advancing 5/8 to 7-1/8 on short-covering.
"Everybody and their brother had shorted that stock," a trader said.
Mexico's ADRs were mostly firmer, with Telmex adding 3/8 to 33-1/8, Televisa up 3/4 at 30-5/8, and Empresas ICA rising 1/8 to 15-1/8.
Chile's Andina rose three percent, adding one to 34-3/4, after Coca-Cola Co said it was buying a six percent stake in the bottler with the possibility of increasing its position to 20 percent.
CTC gained 5/8 to 98-1/8, and Enersis was flat at 31-3/4.
Elsewhere, Templeton Russia Fund bounced 1/8 to 21 after shares in Moscow closed mixed with bargain-hunting providing support.
Russian ADRs fell sharply Thursday on news of President Boris Yeltsin's scheduled heart surgery.
